definition: A `Demarcation` fixes a domain of claims. The weak thesis `N.restrict D` applies the strong norm only to claims in scope and in the domain. `N.Concedes D Acceptable c`: c is in the strong scope, outside the domain, acceptable and fails the standard; every concession is a counterexample to the strong norm.
note: Owner method (2026-10-26, #397): for each strong/weak pair, record the criterion that splits the domain and what the weak side concedes. Instances source the criterion where it is attributed (STMT-RESTRICTED-MEASURE-CRITERION).
